extracted.intended_audience: film critics, reviewers, film journalists, and film-studies students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing film reviews and film criticism: what to cover, how to evaluate films, what makes a review useful to readers, and which films merit coverage. Draws on Roger Ebert's three functions and standard journalistic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film Review (purpose and audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aimed at the general public and published soon after release; describes plot, characters, director; offers a rating or recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on informing potential viewers what the movie is about and whether to see it; keep timely relevance; avoid deep scholarly analysis. Match review length to film significance and avoid spoilers for new releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film Criticism (purpose and audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly study, interpretation, and evaluation of films; situates a film in cinema history and broader cultural conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize interpretation, context, and sustained argument rather than immediate consumer guidance; may be published later than a review and can assume a more informed readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Give some notion of what the movie is about and what it is like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize essentials (plot, tone, notable contributors) so a reader can understand the film's subject and style without having seen it; be clear but concise to avoid unnecessary spoilers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey the experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey what it’s like to watch the film, not just deliver a verdict; readers might disagree with the rating but should still be able to make an informed decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sensory, emotional, and tonal qualities: how the film feels, its pacing, atmosphere, and emotional effects; use evocative language so the review communicates the viewing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be worth reading on its own terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should stand as a piece of writing of interest beyond being a simple footnote to a numeric rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide insights, analysis, or stylistic flair so the piece has value even to readers who ignore the star/score; avoid reducing the review to only a verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — what movies get reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors determining which films merit coverage in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical considerations include: theatrical release in major markets; festival debuts (Cannes, Sundance, TIFF); streaming premieres of significant projects; major directors or stars; award contenders; alignment with a cultural moment; genre significance; independent/international highlights; anniversary screenings; restorations/4K releases; and distinctive marketing events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — Story / Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the film's storytelling elements and narrative effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the story has a comprehensive arc, plausibility within the film’s internal logic, identifiable themes, a connection between themes and audience, and pacing that fits the film’s tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — Craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the technical and craft elements that realize the film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate direction, acting performances, cinematography, editing rhythm, sound design, music/score, production design, costumes, and visual effects; discuss how these elements support or undermine the film’s aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: How well the film holds and affects an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the film holds attention throughout, delivers emotional resonance, surprises or subverts expectations, and leaves memorable moments or images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — Cinema Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the film’s relationship to genre, auteur, and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the film in genre context, in the director’s oeuvre, and within cultural conversation; evaluate originality versus derivation and identify references or influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often watch films more than once; avoid spoilers for new releases; disclose personal biases or preferences; match review length to the film’s significance; be transparent about viewing circumstances (screeners vs theatrical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Newsworthiness Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying reasons editors and publications prioritize certain films for coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural significance, major release status (budget/distribution), director/star prominence, festival prestige, genre impact, critical anticipation, audience interest (commercial pull), award potential, whether the film will start conversation (controversial or novel), and visual/aesthetic distinction.
